REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - OCTOBER 28, 2021 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
* COVID-19 NOTICE *
To protect public health and safety during the COVID-19 pandemic and in compliance with the current State Department of Public Health and Los Angeles County Health Officer Orders and City of Cerritos COVID-19 Safety Plan, the City Council Chamber will be open to the public. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20, N-29-20, and N-08-21, and subsequently by Assembly Bill 361 (Chapter 165, Statutes of 2021), this meeting may also be conducted via teleconference, if necessary. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in-person in the Council Chamber subject to posted COVID-19 protocols.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY,
OCTOBER 28, 2021, 7:00 P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL,
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Bishop David Montgomery, Church of Jesus Christ of the
  Latter Day Saints.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Grace Hu.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Bruce Barrows
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Chuong Vo
  Mayor/Chair Grace Hu

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  Proclamations were issued by the City Council as follows:

  Hindu Heritage Month (Month of October).

  Law Office of Sam Trivedi and Associates (Business Spotlight).

5B.  Informational update on the City's response to the COVID-19 pandemic and other City
  events, services, and programs.

  An informational report was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian & Marketing Manager.
  A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  There was no further action taken on this item.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Written correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record and full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Dr. Charles Zahedi, submitted written correspondence offering free dental exams for
  Cerritos residents and donation to the City of FDA approved hand sanitizer.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, October 28, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 2 of 8

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  In-person public comments:

  Dr. Amit Desai thanked the City for recognizing October as Hindu Heritage Month and
  spoke regarding the services and contributions provided by the local Hindu community.

  Raj Kumar thanked the City for recognizing October as Hindu Heritage Month.

  Kamal Gupta thanked the City for recognizing October as Hindu Heritage Month and
  requested whether the time period for displaying Diwali lights can be extended by the
  City.

  Vijay Patil thanked the City for recognizing October as Hindu Heritage Month.

  Professor Keshav Patel thanked the City for recognizing October as Hindu Heritage
  Month.

  Ketan Prajapati thanked the City for recognizing October as Hindu Heritage Month.

  Shirley Escobar spoke regarding her experience with Dr. Zahedi and his free mobile
  dental service.

  Colin Choi spoke regarding medication disposal options program and requested the City
  consider a location for a disposal site at the Cerritos Senior Center.

  Jun Santos inquired when the City will be noticing the availability of any vacancies at
  the Emerald Villas and Pioneer Villas senior development.

  Daisy Legasca inquired regarding the creation of a Youth and Senior Affairs Commission.

  Ram Kakkar expressed concern regarding a recent theft on his property and inquired as
  to the current level of law enforcement patrols in the City.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the
  Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to place consideration of the time
  period for allowing holiday lights to be displayed in the community, including Diwali
  holiday lights, on a future City Council agenda.

  CONSENSUS (Vo): Directed the City Manager to place consideration of placing a
  medication disposal site at one or more City facilities on a future City Council agenda.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to place consideration of the sale of
  available units at the Emerald Villas and Pioneer Villas senior housing developments on
  a future City Council agenda.

(minutes continue on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, October 28, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 3 of 8

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Thursday, October 14, 2021, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting
  Minutes (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve the Thursday,
  October 14, 2021, 7:00 p.m., City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated October 28, 2021 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve the
  Register of Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  October 28, 2021  $4,020,545.36 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Award of contract for the printing and mailing of the Cerritos News, Cerritos Library
  News & Cerritos Lifelong Enrichment Combined Newsletter, and Community Services
  Program, Bid No. 1438-21 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Yokoyama, to:

  1. Award a contract for the printing and mailing of the Cerritos News, Cerritos Library
  News & Cerritos Lifelong Enrichment Combined Newsletter, and Community Services
  Program to Southwest Offset Printing in the amount of $76,759.12, with the
  following provisions:

  a. The term of the contract covers twelve (12) months from January 2022 to
  December 2022, with an option to renew in 2023 and 2024 by mutual agreement
  of both parties for two additional twelve (12) month periods. The contract is
  issued on a month-to-month basis. Upon completion of the initial 12-month
  period of the agreement, the vendor may request that the City approve an
  increase in the product cost for work to be completed for the succeeding
  extension period(s). The maximum annual increase for any extension period
  shall be the lesser of either 5 percent or the percentage increase, if any, based
  on the Consumer’s Price Index of the Bureau of Labor Statistics, U.S. Department
  of Labor, Los Angeles – Long Beach – Anaheim metropolitan area for the period
  of July 1 through June 30 of the calendar year immediately preceding the date of
  such adjustment, and
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, October 28, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 4 of 8

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7C.  (continued)

  b. In the event issues of non-performance arise, the project would be removed from
  Southwest Offset Printing and taken to the next lowest qualified bidder to ensure
  the City’s printing deadline, quality standards and specifications are met. This
  process would be repeated as necessary in order of the lowest bid to the highest
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7D.  Adoption of Ordinance:

  Ordinance introduced at the October 14, 2021 City Council Regular Meeting:

  Waive full reading of and adopt Ordinance No. 1036, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF
  CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, ESTABLISHING THE CITY’S GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION
  DATE AS THE SECOND TUESDAY OF APRIL IN EACH EVEN-NUMBERED YEAR AND ADDING
  SECTION 2.40.030 TO THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE PROVIDING FOR THE
  PROCEDURE FOR HOLDING ELECTIONS AS AUTHORIZED BY THE CERRITOS CITY
  CHARTER AND THE CALIFORNIA ELECTIONS CODE, AND REPEALING ORDINANCE 1019
  (COUNCIL).

  This item was pulled from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration at the request
  of Councilmember Yokoyama.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1. Waive full reading of and adopt Ordinance No. 1036, AN ORDINANCE OF THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, ESTABLISHING THE CITY’S GENERAL
  MUNICIPAL ELECTION DATE AS THE SECOND TUESDAY OF APRIL IN EACH
  EVEN-NUMBERED YEAR AND ADDING SECTION 2.40.030 TO THE CERRITOS
  MUNICIPAL CODE PROVIDING FOR THE PROCEDURE FOR HOLDING
  ELECTIONS AS AUTHORIZED BY THE CERRITOS CITY CHARTER AND THE
  CALIFORNIA ELECTIONS CODE, AND REPEALING ORDINANCE 1019
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  Yokoyama
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

(minutes continued on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, October 28, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 5 of 8

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Recommendation by the Cerritos Planning Commission, on a vote of 5-0, to approve the
  following:

  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  OF CERRITOS APPROVING CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT 2021-2, A REQUEST BY THE
  PROPERTY OWNERS TO PERMIT LIGHT INDUSTRIAL WAREHOUSING, WHOLESALING AND
  MANUFACTURING USES AT 10603 MIDWAY AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, 90703. THE
  SUBJECT PROPERTY IS ZONED INDUSTRIAL COMMERCIAL-TWO (MC-2) (APN 7016-005-
  012) (COUNCIL).*

  *Pursuant to Section 15301 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), this
  project is categorically exempt from CEQA review.

  A staff report was given by Sandy Cisneros, Senior Planner. A PowerPoint presentation
  was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments period.

  Jonathan Matson, architect for the property owners, spoke in support of the approval of
  the subject project.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the
  Mayor declared the public comments period and public hearing closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Waive full reading of and adopt Resolution No. 2021-23, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT 2021-2, A
  REQUEST BY THE PROPERTY OWNERS TO PERMIT LIGHT INDUSTRIAL
  WAREHOUSING, WHOLESALING AND MANUFACTURING USES AT 10603
  MIDWAY AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, 90703. THE SUBJECT PROPERTY
  IS ZONED INDUSTRIAL COMMERCIAL-TWO (MC-2) (APN 7016-005-012), to
  include the following addition to the Conditions of Approval:

  e. (Project-Specific Condition of Approval)
  In accordance with Cerritos Municipal Section 22.33.700(11) applicable to the
  MC-2 zone where the subject property is located, no sign shall exceed a height
  greater than thirty feet as measured from the top of the adjacent street curb, nor
  shall any sign be located on the roof or parapet of any building (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

(minutes continued on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, October 28, 2021, 7:00 p.m.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of the continuation of the Cerritos Fine Arts and Historical
  Commission (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kathy Matsumoto, Assistant City Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments period.

  Matt Kauble spoke in support of continuation of the Fine Arts and Historical Commission.

  Janet Beach spoke in support of continuation of the Fine Arts and Historical Commission.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the
  Mayor declared the public comments period and public hearing closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Hu, to continue the Fine Arts and
  Historical Commission with no modification (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of an informational budget and audit compliance report for
  Fiscal Year 2021-22 (COUNCIL).

  Staff reports were given by Jeff Thielke, Budget Manager and Dario Simoes, Assistant
  City Engineer.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period
  closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Barrows, to:

  1. Ratify the executed Budget Amendments from the first quarter of Fiscal Year 2021-
  2022 as summarized in the Budget Adjustment Log included as Exhibit 1 in the
  official agenda report for this item; and

  2. Receive and file the report (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or

  None.

11A.  Report from City Manager/Executive Director

  None.

11B.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports

  Reports were given by Councilmembers Barrows and Yokoyama and Mayor Pro Tem Vo.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to place consideration of amending

  Bill Ihrke, City Attorney, announced the City Council would recess to Closed Session

  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957.6 (COUNCIL)
  Agency Negotiators: Art Gallucci, Bill Ihrke, Pam Lee, Torrey Contreras, and

  Unrepresented Employees: Full-Time Exempt

  The City Council reconvened into open session.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, October 28, 2021, 7:00 p.m.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT:

  Bill Ihrke, City Attorney, reported the City Council convened into Closed Session to
